messages:
Alex: Quick update from the RoPE scaling sweep on Llama/Mixtral/Qwen — running NTK/linear/YARN variants across longctx buckets (2k/8k/16k). Found a consistent perf cliff on Mixtral-8k with NTK after ~6.5k tokens, plus some KV cache thrash on mixed-batch workloads.
Maya: can you paste the minimal repro and the perf numbers?
Alex: repro is in the perf job: `scripts/ropexp/mixtral_ntk_longctx.sh --seq 8000 --variant ntk --batch-dist mixed`. Baseline throughput: 220 tok/s until ~6500, then drops to 60 tok/s; latency p95 spikes x3.
Jonathan: do we see any kernel fallbacks when the cliff hits? If the runtime switches kernel or memory layout that's a clue.
perfbot: benchmark summary (mixtral-8k ntk, mixed batch):
```
0-6400: kernel=kv-optimized-v2, throughput=220 tok/s, mem=11.2GB
6401-6600: kernel=kv-optimized-v2, throughput=130 tok/s, mem=13.8GB
6601-8000: kernel=fallback-blocked, throughput=60 tok/s, mem=19.6GB, OOM-retries=2
```
Li: saw that too — KV cache walks blow up because head_kv packing falls into an odd alignment for our fused-attn kernel. The allocator starts fragmenting and we hit a slow path that re-materializes KV.
Maya: any difference between linear vs ntk vs yarn configs?
Alex: linear didn't hit the cliff on Mixtral-8k; NTK did. YARN was in-between — throughput degraded gradually, no sudden cliff. For Qwen-16k NTK behaved fine; Llama-8k had only a modest drop. So model-specific safe ranges matter.
Jonathan: what about batching heuristics? Were we using continuous batching + prefix cache? Mixed-batch workloads can expose cache eviction thrash.
Alex: yes, test used continuous batching + prefix caching enabled. Mixed batch = {single-stream:60%, multi-stream:40%}. When many short and one long request coexist, the KV cache sees many different prefixes and our LRU churns.
Li: added a flamegraph from the failing run: heavy time in `kv_rehydrate_slow_path` and `cuda_memcopy_chunked`. Looks like the kernel tries to re-layout KV for fused attention and triggers a memcpy per head.
Sara: can you share numeric per-model "safe range" suggestions? We should start documenting them in the model catalog and have the scheduler prefer safer variants for longctx.
Alex: provisional safe ranges from the sweep (feel free to dispute):
- Mixtral-8k: linear safe up to 8k; NTK safe up to 6k; YARN safe up to 7k
- Llama-8k: linear and NTK safe up to 7k; YARN safe to 8k
- Qwen-16k: NTK safe to 14k; linear safe to 12k; YARN safe to 15k
(These are throughput-preservation thresholds where throughput stays within 15% of short-ctx baseline and no p95 jump.)
Maya: how were perplexity/quality metrics affected across variants? Any quality regression with linear vs ntk?
Alex: for Mixtral-8k, NTK had slightly lower perplexity at 6k but after the cliff the model starts truncating attention windows (due to kernel fallback) and generation artifacts increase — measurable BLEU/QA-EM drops ~2-4 points in edge cases. Linear kept stable quality but slightly worse perplexity at 4-6k compared to NTK.
Jonathan: actionable items?
Alex: my proposal:
1) runtime: add a soft guard that detects KV re-layout mem pressure and routes new long requests to linear kernel variant for affected model+seq combos.
2) batching: adjust heuristics to avoid mixing many short and single very long in same batch; enforce a max-long-per-batch=1 policy for vulnerable configs.
3) model catalog: publish safe ranges and preferred kernel variant per model+ctx.
4) infra: add a perf check in CI that runs short stress at sequence cutpoints (e.g., 6k,7k,8k) for Mixtral and fail fast on >2x p95 jump.
Li: +1. I'll prototype detection in the allocator to tag the slow-path and emit a metric `kv_relayout_count`. We can add a rollout rule to pivot kernel when metric > threshold.
Sara: I'll update the model catalog draft and add a per-model note under "runtime tuning". Also pinging GTM for any customer-facing notes if we plan a rollback/fallback policy.
Maya: can we get a short replayable run (10m) that hits the cliff deterministically? I want to run profiler and kernel logs.
Alex: yes — I'll queue a run with fixed mixed-batch pattern, seed=42, and attach perf traces. ETA 30m.
perfbot: perf job queued: job_id=perf-mixtral-1768504321-01, link: https://perf.redwood/jobs/perf-mixtral-1768504321-01
Sara: thanks all. Please drop the final safe-range numbers + mitigation PRs in the #eng-runtime follow-up thread. :thumbsup:
